newsitem.title: GERMANY: Welteke-hard to reconcile EMU goals with tax cuts.
newsitem.headline: Welteke-hard to reconcile EMU goals with tax cuts.

text.p: Bundesbank council member Ernst Welteke said on Monday that it was hard to reconcile talk in Germany of a 30 billion mark ($17 billion) package of tax cuts with meeting the deficit criteria for European economic and monetary union (EMU).

Welteke, speaking at an event organised by the Association of Foreign Banks, also criticised the public debate over whether Germany could fulfil the deficit target, saying Europe had made great progress on monetary convergence.
"I find it difficult to understand how we can talk on the one hand of 30 billion marks of tax reductions and at the same time of meeting the three percent deficit criteria," Welteke said in a speech.
Would-be EMU members are supposed to cut their budget deficits to three precent of gross domestic product (GDP).

Germany's opposition-controlled upper house of parliament, the Bundesrat, on Friday rejected Finance Minister Theo Waigel's tax reforms for 1998 and 1999, sending the bills to parliament's mediation committee.

The 1998 and 1999 tax bills, which envisage net tax cuts of 30 billion marks, last week passed comfortably in the lower house with the backing of deputies from the ruling coalition. ($ = 1.747 German Marks)
